cited.quote: was taken up and completed, vide G.O.(Ms) No.214, Revenue and Disaster Management Department, dated 17.05.2022
committed to revitalizing the major waterways of Chennai including Adyar, Coovum, Buckingham canal, and Kosasthalaiyar

rationale: C2 reports storm water drain works to prevent flood damage sanctioned by GO dated 17.05.2022 and later GOs, covering the drainage component. River deepening appears only as plans (C3 Adyar restoration 'will undergo'), and no Rs.5000 crore programme is shown. C1 and C4 are budget plans and a water security study.

cited.quote: permit the sale of Palm Jaggery through select Fair Price Shops run by Cooperatives
From October 2021 to March 2024, Palm Jaggery worth Rs.162.15 lakh has been sold through the Fair Price Shops.

rationale: C1 is the GO dated 30.09.2021 permitting sale of palm jaggery to cardholders in fair price shops, but only through select shops on a pilot basis. C3 (2024) still describes sale through select shops, with sales since October 2021. Implemented with reduced coverage.

cited.quote: Special Incentive to Sugarcane Farmers at Rs.150/- per M.T. for 2020-21 crushing season
sugar cane price has increased to Rs.3,135/MT and an amount of Rs.250 crore has been allocated

rationale: C4 is the GO (06.12.2021) sanctioning a special incentive raising the cane price to Rs.2,900. C2 shows later incentives raised the price only to Rs.3,135/MT by 2023-24, well short of Rs.4,000. C5 only maintained Rs.2,750. Price raised but by a materially smaller amount.

cited.quote: For setting up drip irrigation in sugarcane cultivation, 100% subsidy to small and marginal farmers and 75% subsidy to other
During the year 2025-26, Micro Irrigation system will be installed over an area of 3 lakh acres

rationale: C1 describes a drip subsidy for sugarcane only, with a different structure (100%/75%), not a 90% subsidy for up to 5 acres. C2 is a budget plan for micro irrigation. C3, C4 and C5 concern solar pumps, electric motor pumps and horticulture. No official step for the promised subsidy.

cited.quote: the Government has enhanced the fishing ban relief assistance from Rs.5,000/- to Rs.8,000/-
For the year 2024-25, the Government have disbursed a sum of Rs.142.68 crore to 1,78,362 fishermen

rationale: C1 and C2 report that the fishing ban relief was raised from Rs.5,000 to Rs.8,000 following the 18.08.2023 announcement. C1 shows 2023-24 disbursement still at the old rate. C2 shows 2024-25 disbursement at the new rate. No GO date is given, so the year comes from C2.
